question: The Special Economic Zones Act, 2005, was passed by the Indian Parliament in________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**May **2005__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Special Economic Zones (SEZ) Act, 2005** was passed by the **Indian Parliament in May 2005**, to promote economic growth through the establishment of SEZs.
 
• The Act provides a **comprehensive legal framework** for the development, operation, and management of SEZs in India.
 
• The primary objective of the SEZ Act is to **attract foreign direct investment (FDI)**, promote **exports**, and generate **employment opportunities**.
 
• SEZs are designated areas that offer **special tax incentives** and simplified regulations to foster industrial growth and investment.
 
• As of 2022, there are approximately **250 operational SEZs in India**, contributing significantly to India's **industrial development** and **export growth**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Features of the SEZ Act, 2005:**

 
 
• Provides **tax exemptions** on profits derived from export activities for a specified period.
 
• Allows **single-window clearance** for approvals to reduce bureaucratic delays.
 
• Permits **100% Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** in the manufacturing sector within SEZs.
 
• Exempts businesses in SEZs from **customs duties, central excise duties, service tax**, and other levies.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of the SEZ Act:**
 
 
• Encourage **export-oriented industries** by creating a conducive environment for trade and commerce.
 
• Provide **world-class infrastructure** to boost industrial development.
 
• Create **large-scale employment opportunities** for the local population.
 
• Enhance India's competitiveness in the **global market** by attracting investment.
 
 
 
• **Impact of SEZs in India:**
 
 
• SEZs have significantly contributed to India's export growth, particularly in sectors like **information technology, pharmaceuticals, and textiles**.
 
• They have facilitated **regional development** by attracting investments to less-developed areas.
 
• Prominent SEZs in India include **Noida SEZ, Santa Cruz SEZ (for electronics), and Kandla SEZ**.
 
 
 
• **Challenges Faced by SEZs:**
 
 
• Issues related to **land acquisition** and opposition from local communities.
 
• Underperformance in meeting targeted levels of **employment and investment** in some SEZs.
 
• Concerns over **tax revenue losses** due to exemptions provided to SEZ developers and businesses.
 
 
 
• **Global Perspective:**
 
 
• Countries like **China** and **Dubai** have successfully utilized SEZs for economic growth.
 
• **China's Shenzhen SEZ** is a prime example, transforming it into a global economic hub.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Special Economic Zones (SEZs):**

 
 
• SEZs are **designated areas** with relaxed economic regulations to boost industrial and economic development.
 
• They are focused on **export-oriented industries** and provide **tax benefits** to businesses operating within them.
 
• The SEZ policy was introduced in **2000**, while the **SEZ Act** was enacted in **2005**.
 
 
 
• **Legal Framework:**
 
 
• The SEZ Act ensures that operations comply with **national and international trade laws**.
 
• It simplifies the process for **industrial investment** and enhances **ease of doing business**.
 
 
 
• **Future Prospects:**
 
 
• Improved infrastructure and policies could help SEZs attract more **foreign investments**.
 
• Addressing challenges like **land acquisition** and tax concerns will further enhance their effectiveness.
